extraction_text: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma about the origin, nature, and rewards of the donation called 'Jyotis'.
Bhishma explains that this question is answered through an ancient conversation between Manu and Suvarna.
The sage Suvarna, known for his golden complexion, meets Manu on Mount Meru.
Suvarna asks Manu why people worship gods with flowers and other offerings, and what rewards this brings.
Manu explains that this question is answered through another ancient conversation between Shukra and Bali.
Shukra (descendant of Bhrigu) visits Bali (son of Virochana), the king of Asuras who rules the three worlds.
Bali asks Shukra about the rewards of worshipping gods with flowers, incense, lamps, and other offerings.
Shukra explains that austerity came first, then righteousness, and between them appeared climbing plants and herbs.
Shukra describes how plants have different natures - some beneficial, some poisonous, some neutral - all having Soma as their soul.
Flowers are described as 'pleasing to the mind' and bring happiness and blessings.

attributes.action: Explaining the nature and benefits of flowers

extraction_text: Virtuous and pure people offer flowers to deities, pleasing the deities.
One who chooses their deity and offers flowers with a wish for blessings attains happiness.
Classification of plants and trees based on energy, taste (pungent, mild, strong), and suitability for sacrificial use.
Different garlands are preferred by Asuras (demons), Devas (gods), Yakshas (nature spirits), Rakshasas (demons), ancestors, and people.

attributes.action: Listing preferences of different beings for garlands

extraction_text: Description of flowers based on origin (forests, villages, cultivated trees, mountains), presence of thorns, and differences in smell, taste, color, and shape.
Tradition states flowers have two types of smells: pleasant and unpleasant; pleasant-smelling flowers should be offered to deities.

extraction_text: Thornless trees and flowers, often white, are always favored by the gods.
